research_rationale: Executive Order 11545 of July 9, 1970 (35 FR 11161) established the Defense Distinguished Service Medal under the President's authority as Commander in Chief; it rests on no statute, has no own-terms end, and sets no deadline, sunset or condition. The held original (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11545.txt, an official Federal Register text) contains four numbered sections and no other operative paragraph. The one held later instrument that names it is Executive Order 14085 of October 3, 2022 (87 FR 60541), section 6, which amends sections 1 and 2 by strike-and-insert and leaves sections 3 and 4 untouched; under the strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21 the amended clauses continue until the parent order ends. The current U.S. Code (10 U.S.C. 1125 note, "Ex. Ord. No. 11545. Defense Distinguished Service Medal") reproduces all four sections as amended by Executive Order 14085, which shows the order operative in its amended form in the edition current through 2026-10-09. Machine searches of the U.S. Code, the eCFR and the Federal Register disposition catalog (read for coverage) found no revocation, supersession or termination. The held OCR of section 4 of the original omits words (a line after "when so" is missing); the Code note supplies the full text, and the clause is judged on that complete text. Original not authenticated beyond the held Federal Register text; no page images were inspected, none being required for this source.
savings_reason: The order is not terminated: the current U.S. Code note reproduces sections 1 to 4 as amended through Executive Order 14085, so there is no repealed or ended command for a savings clause to preserve; the bounded searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, Federal Register disposition catalog) found no ending instrument whose savings effect needs tracing.
earlier_end_check: The held original has no until, expiry, report or condition language. A search of the held corpus for the number 11545 (LOOKUPS number citations: Executive Order 14085, its Federal Register copy, the 1989 OFR codification note and the Code) found only the amendment in section 6 of Executive Order 14085, not a revocation, supersession or termination. The U.S. Code, eCFR and Federal Register catalog searches record no ending event. No earlier end exists on the held evidence.
scope_check: Sections 1 to 4 are the complete operative inventory: section 1 establishes the medal and who may receive it, section 2 sets design and precedence regulations, section 3 limits the medal to one per person with devices for later service, section 4 permits posthumous award. The order has no preamble command, no savings clause and no section after section 4. Executive Order 14085 section 6(a) amends section 1 ("military officer" becomes "member of the Armed Forces of the United States") and section 6(b) amends section 2 ("he" becomes "the Secretary"); sections 3 and 4 are unamended.
independent_command_check: Each of the four sections is a separate command or authorization (establishment and eligibility; design, regulations and precedence; one-medal limit and devices; posthumous award). The 2022 amendments change only the eligible class in section 1 and a pronoun in section 2, so each section keeps its own current predicate in the Code note that reproduces all four.
savings_check: The order is unrevoked and unterminated, so no savings question arises for any clause. The held current text records no accrued-rights or repeal provision touching it.

research_rationale: Executive Order 11593 of May 13, 1971 (36 FR 8921), Protection and Enhancement of the Cultural Environment, sets a federal policy of leadership in preserving the historic and cultural environment (section 1), assigns federal agency heads duties to inventory and nominate eligible properties, protect them in the interim, record them before alteration, maintain them, submit procedures annually and cooperate with transferees (section 2), and assigns the Secretary of the Interior supporting duties (section 3). It is issued under the President's authority "in furtherance of the purposes and policies" of four statutes (NEPA, the National Historic Preservation Act of 1966, the Historic Sites Act of 1935 and the Antiquities Act of 1906), none of which is the order's sole source of authority; the order contains no sentence that makes it depend on a statute's continuation, and no held source shows any of those statutes repealed. The held original is an official Federal Register OCR text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11593.txt). It contains dates (July 1, 1973 for inventories; January 1, 1972 and annually thereafter for procedures) and one contingent phrase (interim caution until inventories are completed), but each is a deadline, schedule or stage within a continuing duty, not an expiry; under the 2026-10-28 ruling a deadline is not an end and no held source shows any agency duty completed or withdrawn. No held later instrument amends, revokes or supersedes the order: the lookup of held texts citing the number found Executive Orders 13006 (May 21, 1996) and 13022 (October 31, 1996), which recite it as policy to be followed ("in furtherance of and consistent with" it; "consistent with the policy stated in Executive Order 11593") and neither amends nor revokes it; agency notices and a 2026 rule (91 FR 8072) that list it among authorities followed; the 1989 OFR codification entry; and the Code note under 54 U.S.C. 300101 that prints the order unchanged. The three bounded searches were read for coverage: the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, through 2026-10-09) hit two places, the eCFR search (as of 2026-10-14) hit 78 regulation passages that cite the order, and the Federal Register disposition catalog search hit only the cross references from Executive Orders 13006 and 13022. No ending was found. The current basis for each clause is the held original read with those searches; the Code note is a context source that the checker cannot quote-verify, so it is not cited as the source.
savings_reason: The order is not terminated and no held instrument limits it; the 1996 orders that cite it treat it as continuing policy, so there is no ended command whose accrued effects need savings treatment.
earlier_end_check: No clause has an own-terms end. The dated provisions are deadlines or schedules (July 1, 1973; January 1, 1972 and annually thereafter) and one interim phrase tied to completion of inventories, and no held source dates the completion of every agency's inventories or shows the annual submissions stopped. A search of held texts for the number 11593 found only recitals (Executive Orders 13006 and 13022), the 1989 OFR line, agency notices and rules citing it as an authority, and the Code note; none revokes or supersedes it, and the catalog search recorded only the two cross references. The two recitals neither amend nor revoke any section of this order, so they are not recorded as later events.
scope_check: The inventory has 17 clauses and no preamble command beyond the recital of authority: section 1; section 2 with subsections (a) to (f); section 3 with subsections (a) to (h). The dossier inventory was checked against the held original, which ends with subsection 3(h) and the signature line; no clause is missing and none is merged.
independent_command_check: Each subsection of sections 2 and 3 is a separate duty with its own actor and subject (inventory, interim caution, recording, maintenance, annual procedures, cooperation with transferees; encouraging surveys, criteria, nomination review, liaison officers, information, advice, transferee-plan review, review of agency procedures), so the apparent completion of one (for example the 1973 inventory deadline) would not end another. No held source ends any of them.
savings_check: The order is unrevoked, so no clause ended and no savings question arises. The two recitals in Executive Orders 13006 and 13022 rely on it as continuing policy.

research_rationale: Executive Order 11755 of December 29, 1973 (39 FR 779) permits Federal contractors to employ non-Federal prison inmates on paid work release when listed conditions are met (section 1), requires the Attorney General to certify, and after notice and hearing to revoke certification of, a jurisdiction's work-release laws (sections 1(a)(2) and 1(b)), directs revision of the procurement regulations (section 2), supersedes Executive Order 325A (section 3) and takes effect January 1, 1974 (section 4). It was issued under the President's own authority; the preamble recited 18 U.S.C. 4082, since replaced, but Executive Order 12943 of December 13, 1994 rewrote that recital to cite 18 U.S.C. 3621 and 3622 and the Bureau of Prisons, so no repealed-statute dependency is left in the order as amended. The held original is an official Federal Register OCR text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11755.txt) with irregular letter spacing, so no quotation from it is used. Two held later orders amend it by amendment, not ending: Executive Order 12608 section 23 (September 9, 1987) adds the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands to the territories listed in section 1(a), and Executive Order 12943 (December 13, 1994) rewrites the second preamble paragraph and adds subsection 1(c) excluding micropurchases. Under the strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21 each amended clause continues, amended, with the parent order. The current basis for every operative clause is the held original read with the three bounded searches, whose coverage notes were read. As context only, 28 CFR 0.94-1(b) (eCFR text amended through 2026-10-27, held in the packet as a custody record, so not cited as a source) delegates to the Director of the Bureau of Justice Assistance the Attorney General's power under the order to certify and revoke certification of work-release laws. The searches: the U.S. Code search (release point 119-121, through 2026-10-09) hit one note, the printed order as amended through Executive Order 12943 under 18 U.S.C. 3622 note; the eCFR search (as of 2026-10-14) hit eight regulations, including 28 CFR 0.94-1 and the Federal Acquisition Regulation sections that apply the order; the Federal Register disposition catalog search hit the two amendments. No revocation, supersession or own-terms end was found. Section 3 (supersession of Executive Order 325A) was complete when the order took effect.
savings_reason: The order is not revoked or terminated; only section 3 (supersession of Executive Order 325A) was spent, on January 1, 1974, with no saving language, and the held bounded searches found no instrument ending the remaining sections, so no residual savings question arises beyond the unreserved supersession of the earlier order.
earlier_end_check: The held original has no until, expiry, report-deadline or condition-subsequent language; its only dated terms are the signing date, the January 1, 1974 effective date and the supersession of Executive Order 325A. A search of held texts for the number 11755 found the two amending orders, the 1989 OFR codification entry, FAR rulemakings and clauses, 28 CFR 0.94-1 and the Code note; none revokes or supersedes the order, and the catalog search recorded only the two amendments. One FR text found by number (FR Doc. 04-16785, a Bureau of Prisons or FAR document) is cited as a FAR change and is not an ending. No earlier end exists for sections 1, 1(a)(1), 1(a)(2), 1(b), 2 or 4 on the held evidence; section 3 ended on its own terms on January 1, 1974.
scope_check: The inventory covers the seven operative provisions after the preamble: section 1 (stipulation in contracts and the parole, probation and pardoned-person proviso, including the voluntary-pay and consultation conditions), item 1(a)(1) (conditions A to D), item 1(a)(2) (Attorney General certification), subsection 1(b) (revocation of certification), section 2 (revision of regulations), section 3 (supersession of Executive Order 325A) and section 4 (effective date). The preamble paragraphs recite findings and the intent to replace Executive Order 325A and issue no command. Subsection 1(c), added by Executive Order 12943, and the Northern Mariana Islands words added by Executive Order 12608 are later amendments of section 1, recorded as later events, not original clauses.
independent_command_check: Section 1 (stipulation requirement), 1(a)(2) (certification) and 1(b) (revocation of certification) are separate commands operating on different actors (contracting agencies, the Attorney General). Section 2 directs the procurement regulations to be revised and is separate from them. Sections 3 and 4 concern Executive Order 325A and the effective date. The end of section 3 on January 1, 1974 does not affect sections 1, 2 or 4.
savings_check: The order has no savings clause, and section 3 supersedes Executive Order 325A without reserving anything, so any question about contracts that were under the old stipulation is outside the clauses of this order that remain operative. No held later instrument ends or limits any section of this order.

research_rationale: Executive Order 11851 of April 10, 1975 (40 FR 16645) delegates to the Secretary of the Treasury, with the concurrence of the Secretary of State and the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations, authority to issue regulations preventing importation of certain European Community cheeses on which export restitution payments were made, to implement a December 1974 agreement, and lets agency heads redelegate (section 2). It rests on section 204 of the Agricultural Act of 1956, 7 U.S.C. 1854, and 3 U.S.C. 301, neither of which the order or any held source shows to have been repealed; the Code section 7 U.S.C. 1854 is itself current (its text is held in the repository at jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t7-s1854.txt, which is not a registered packet source and is mentioned only as context). The held original (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11851.txt, an official Federal Register OCR text with irregular letter spacing) has no own-terms end, expiry, deadline or condition. The order has no later amending or revoking instrument: the Federal Register disposition catalog search found none, the lookup of held texts citing the number found only the 1989 OFR codification entry and a 19 CFR 12.6 text that cites the order as the source of the restitution-payment affidavit, and the U.S. Code note under 7 U.S.C. 1854 reproduces the order (current release point 119-121, through 2026-10-09) with the bracketed editorial update "[now United States Trade Representative]", showing it is still printed as in force. The eCFR search recorded two hits including 19 CFR 12.6 (held at jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/cfr-t19-12.6.txt, not a registered packet source), whose text still requires affidavits that cheese has not received "restitution payments of the type referred to in Executive Order No. 11851"; it is context for the continuing predicate, not the cited basis.
savings_reason: The order is not terminated: the Code note under 7 U.S.C. 1854 still reproduces sections 1 and 2, no held source revokes or limits them, and the bounded searches found no ending instrument, so there is no ended command whose accrued effects a savings clause would preserve.
earlier_end_check: The held text has no until, effective-date, report or expiry language. Searches of held texts for the number 11851 found only the 1989 OFR codification line, 19 CFR 12.6 and the Code note, none of which revokes, supersedes or limits the order; the later-events catalog search had zero hits. No earlier end exists on the held evidence. A delegation of authority to issue regulations is a continuing authorization, not a one-time act exhausted by issuing the 1975 regulation (T.D. 75-210, later amended in 2015 per the 19 CFR 12.6 source line).
scope_check: The order has two sections and no other operative paragraph: section 1 (authorization with subparagraphs (a) and (b) defining the regulations) and section 2 (redelegation, with the limit that the Treasury regulation-issuing function may be redelegated only to officials appointed with Senate advice and consent, as provided by 3 U.S.C. 301). The OCR of the Federal Register text breaks the closing citation "301." into a separate fragment; the inventory is corrected so that fragment is part of section 2.
independent_command_check: Section 1 (lead-in), 1(a), 1(b) and section 2 are separate statements of authority: who may issue regulations, which importations (into the Customs Territory except Puerto Rico; into Puerto Rico when for transshipment) the regulations may reach, and who may redelegate. None depends on another ending; the Code note reproduces all of them.
savings_check: The order is unrevoked and unterminated, so no clause ends and no savings question arises. The only held later regulation (19 CFR 12.6) applies the delegated authority; it is not an ending.

research_rationale: Executive Order 11884 of October 7, 1975 (40 FR 47469) prescribes the official coat of arms, seal, and flag of the Vice President (sections 1 to 4), declares that these designs shall represent the Vice President exclusively, and revokes Executive Order 10016 of November 10, 1948 (section 5). The held original (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11884.txt, an official Federal Register OCR text with irregular letter spacing and the attached flag specifications) has no deadline, expiry, condition or other own-terms end, and rests on the President's own authority, not a statute that could lapse. No held current-law record (U.S. Code note or eCFR text) names the order, so the current predicate rests on the held original read with the three bounded machine searches, each of which returned zero hits for this order: the U.S. Code search (every citation of the order by number in the text and notes of the titles read, edition current through 2026-10-09), the eCFR search (point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 and GovInfo CFR bulk XML) and the Federal Register disposition catalog search (6942 catalog records naming the order as amended, revoked, superseded or otherwise affected, plus operative sentences in saved order texts). The held later-events chain is empty and the 1989 OFR codification entry only locates the order. Absence of a located amendment or revocation is therefore the whole basis for the continuing finding; it is a bounded-search result, not an affirmative current-law source. The one command that was performed and spent is section 5's revocation of Executive Order 10016, effective on the order's signing.
savings_reason: Section 5 revokes Executive Order 10016 in a single act complete on October 7, 1975, with no saving language; the designs in sections 1 to 4 are not revoked and need no savings clause, and the bounded searches found no instrument that ended or amended them.
earlier_end_check: Sections 1 to 4 contain no own-terms end. A search of held texts for the number 11884 found only the 1989 OFR codification entry (which locates the order and records no amendment or revocation), and the later-events catalog search had zero hits, so no earlier revocation, supersession or amendment is held. Section 5 revokes Executive Order 10016 with the words "is hereby revoked." and takes effect immediately; that one-time command was complete on October 7, 1975 (the order's date, the filing date being the same day), so it has its own first end on that date by the order's own terms.
scope_check: Six clauses: the enacting clause (authority recital and order to proceed as follows), section 1 (coat of arms design: shield and crest), section 2 (seal: the coat of arms encircled by the words Vice President of the United States), section 3 (color and flag), section 4 (designs as described and as set forth in the attached illustrations and specifications, which are made a part of the order; use to represent the Vice President exclusively) and section 5 (immediate effectiveness; revocation of Executive Order 10016). The attached flag specifications and proportions printed on the following Federal Register pages are incorporated by section 4 and are judged with that clause.
independent_command_check: Sections 1, 2 and 3 each prescribe a different emblem (arms, seal, flag) and section 4 independently confines all three designs to representing the Vice President; none depends on another ending. Section 5 is a separate revocation of an earlier order and does not control the designs. The revocation of Executive Order 10016 is performed; the surviving consequence (Executive Order 10016 stays revoked) is a status, not a continuing command of this order.
savings_check: The order contains no savings clause. Section 5 revokes Executive Order 10016 without reserving rights; the held text of Executive Order 10016 was not needed because no clause of this order depends on it. No held source shows a later instrument touching the designs.
